subject: question about spatio-temporal interactions in Blangiardo Cameletti 2012 papers

messages.author: 778bd0cef6c473fc
messages.subject: question about spatio-temporal interactions in Blangiardo Cameletti 2012 papers
parts:
Hello,

I am following the examples in Blangiardo, Cameletti et al. 2012, "Spatial and Spatio-Temporal models with R-INLA”. I have a very simple question relating to the examples contained within that paper.


Following Eq 6 (p. 13) and the code for the “formula.1” model on p. 15, I wrote the model below for my data. There are eight years of data.

formula.1<- y ~ 1 + f(ID.area, model="bym", graph=adjGraph) + x1 + x2 + x3 + f(ID.area1, year, model="iid") + year


mod1 <- inla(formula.1, family=”poisson”, data=data, E=Exp, control.compute=list(dic=TRUE, cpo=TRUE), control.predictor=list(compute=TRUE))


## random effects associated with space-time interaction term ##

rfx.IDarea1 <- mod1$summary.random$ID.area1


Based on the explanation provided by Blangiardo/Cameletti, I understand that the above model has a linear trend (global time effect) and an area-specific trend (via the space-time interaction).  


Here, the random effects for the space-time interaction only have one random effect for each area. The example Georgia births space-time interaction model has a non-linear time term - the inla.make.lincombs command is used - and there is one random effect for each area-year combination. Do I need to use inla.make.lincombs here, even though the time term is linear? And in “my” model, is there only one random effect per area for the space-time interaction because the main time trend in the model is linear?

 

I am just trying to understand these models, starting with the simplest. Thank you for your help!


Mercedes
